thread:
Joanne: Heads up — Ops reported a KV cache eviction spike in eu-west-1 during the v2.1.0 canary run. Pausing the canary now. Will coordinate rollback/pin + new window here.
DeployBot: @Joanne paused deployment 'release/v2.1.0' at 2026-03-20T21:06:12Z. Reason: incident - kv-cache-evictions (eu-west-1). Current state: canary paused, rollout blocked. Suggested automated actions: pin to previous image, disable batching experiment.
Sanjay: Do we need a full rollback or can we pin traffic to v2.0.9 and continue diagnostics?
Micah: Prefer pin+diagnose. I don't see evidence the code change alone caused the evictions — could be kernel-level KV optimizer on a recent kernel patch. Pin to v2.0.9, run trimmed repro load, then decide rollback.
DeployBot: Suggested CLI to enact pin/hard-hold:
```
deployctl hold --release=release/v2.1.0 --by=Joanne --reason="kv-cache-evict"
deployctl pin --cluster=eu-canary --image=v2.0.9
```
Ops Oncall: We saw 4xx->5xx spike starting 21:00, peaked 21:03, partial recovery after circuit backoff at 21:07. No sustained backend errors after 21:10 but KV miss rate stayed ~2x baseline. We're keeping alerts open.
Elise: I'll update the release notes and add a short advisory for customers who hit higher latencies in eu-west. Also creating a rollout-status board card.
Andrew: Does this impact Dedicated customers in eu? Need to check contracts before we move anything there.
Micah: No Dedicated impact observed — only hosted canary nodes in eu-west-1. Confirmed with infra: Dedicated pools are on separate images and infra-level isolation.
Sanjay: Ok plan: 1) Pin eu-canary to v2.0.9 (immediate) 2) Run targeted repro with smaller QPS and KV cache diagnostics 3) If repro shows a clear regression, schedule rollback; otherwise fix kernel/ops settings and retry canary in a maintenance window 4) Notify AE if Dedicated affected.
Joanne: Booking change window: 2026-03-21 02:00-04:00 UTC for the controlled retry (smaller batchsize, kvcache patch toggles). I'll send calendar invite + prod-change ticket.
Elise: I'll post an update to #customer-status and add a short note to the release notes: "Canary paused due to increased KV cache evictions in EU; targeted retry scheduled 02:00 UTC."
DeployBot: Actioned: hold confirmed, pin job queued to eu-canary -> v2.0.9 (job id 61522).
Sanjay: Great. Micah, can you run the postmortem testset in the morning and drop logs into the incident ticket?
Micah: Yep — I'll run regressions + KV diagnostic harness at 01:30 UTC and attach results.
Joanne: Thanks everyone. If anything changes before the window, update this thread. :thumbsup:
Andrew: I'll let sales/support know the short advisory and keep them on standby in case any enterprise tenants ask.
Elise: Adding owners to the change ticket: Joanne (ENG), Micah (ML/Infra), Ops Oncall.
Micah: One more note — if we need a rollforward instead of rollback, the plan is to push a tiny kernel-level config patch to canary nodes and re-enable new batching feature behind a feature flag. We'll validate with 10% traffic first.
Joanne: Sounds good. Closing coordination notes here; will reopen if we opt for rollback. :white_check_mark:
